summary: Router 0.42.0: the content check before a cloud tier (privacy.py, called only from proxy._Relay._via_cloud when cloud.needs_privacy_check holds) gets context redactors per tool format (redactors.py: ha_assist = the previous Home Assistant code moved unchanged, generic_json = configured dotted paths/keys) and locale packs (privacy_locale.py: ch-de = the previous patterns, keywords, refusal and marker, default; en = e-mail/phone/IBAN, English keywords). Implements ADR-0119 (proposed in #177) and adds ADR-0125 (unrecognised tool results pass by default; keep_local is an explicit switch). Traced B6: the verdict body is still what cloud.run sends; a refused or unredacted verdict returns the refusal before cloud.run; the redaction runs on a deep copy; redact_tools is applied before any redactor, so choosing other redactors cannot drop it. B7 unchanged: classifier call, loopback endpoint check and fail-closed handling are untouched. Default behaviour verified byte-identical (recorded corpus of 35 synthetic payloads from the base commit's privacy.py; 12,000 randomized synthetic payloads compared against origin/main privacy.py, 0 differences). The new keys are config.yaml only (not in settings.EDITABLE, asserted by test). Load-time refusals prevent configurations that look configured but redact nothing (empty/unknown/duplicate redactors, generic_json without its redactor and vice versa, malformed paths, unknown locale or mode). /admin/state shows generic_json only as counts. Found and fixed during the review: generic_json walks JSON recursively, so a deeply nested tool result could exhaust the stack; it now checks depth iteratively (limit 100) and treats deeper JSON as unredactable (request stays local). The pre-existing RecursionError of json.loads on extremely deep JSON (it reached the unexpected-error middleware as a 500 under ha_assist) now keeps the request local with the refusal; no payload left in either case. Regexes of the en pack use only bounded quantifiers. No secrets, hostnames or personal data added; test data is synthetic (example domains, published example IBANs, fictional UK/NANP numbers).

tests.evidence: 117 checks ALL OK: default corpus byte-identical (35 cases), every ch-de pattern and keyword group blocks, every default domain/device class/listed tool redacted, too-deep JSON stays local, en hits and non-hits, generic_json paths/keys/*/depth limit, named non-JSON stays local, keep_local mode, 13 refused configurations, nothing editable from the web UI, proxy refusal without provider call. Fault injection (AHV pattern removed; default mode flipped to keep_local) made it fail with 3 and 9 failures.

limitations: python test/check_adr_index.py was run and reports one finding: ADR numbers not consecutive, because ADR-0105 to ADR-0124 belong to other open pull requests of the same series and ADR-0125 was assigned to this one. The index table was regenerated with --write and matches the files; the check passes once the earlier PRs are merged.
With the default unrecognised_tool_results: pass, tool results in formats no redactor knows still reach the provider unredacted (pre-existing; now documented, keep_local available).
No openHAB or ioBroker redactor: their tool-result formats could not be verified with real data.
The privacy classifier stays German/English (ADR-0077); the en pack's patterns are heuristics checked by test sentences, not a DLP guarantee.
The end-to-end suite does not cover the privacy path; it is covered by self-tests with fakes for classifier and provider.
ADR-0119 is proposed on another branch (#177); this change implements it and records one deviation in ADR-0125 for the maintainer to decide.
